title: fix: deliver mentions to guest inboxes
body: ## What Problem This Solves A profile limited to session scopes can be eligible to read a conversation while still being excluded as a mention recipient. Its own Inbox methods also require broad read access, and the targeted change notification is filtered out before reaching the browser. Together, these gates prevent an eligible guest from receiving and managing a mention through the existing Inbox. This recipient and Inbox contribution builds on the sender and lookup support merged in #178038. Related sender lookup context is in #178031. ## User Impact Eligible signed-in guests can receive automatic Inbox updates, list their currently accessible mentions, and dismiss their own entries using `operator.sessions.read` or the read access implied by `operator.sessions.write`. Current profile, role, and conversation visibility continue to govern every read and dismissal. Another profile cannot select that guest's Inbox or dismiss its entries, and a mention does not grant conversation access or membership. This uses the existing Inbox and replay records. It introduces no configuration or storage migration. Optional browser/OS push retains its existing subscription and permission requirements; the change concerns the live Inbox. ## Why This Change Was Made The recipient policy now uses the same session-read scope implication as the sender path. The shared method mapping gives the profile-owned `mentions.list` and `mentions.dismiss` methods their narrow admission alternative, which the existing UI capability check also consumes. The existing `mentions.changed` event remains a targeted invalidation containing a Gateway identity and view revision. The broadcaster admits it to session readers only through the targeted personal-invalidation path. The Inbox still selects the current authenticated recipient and filters entries through current conversation access. The sidebar's health and cron inventory guards remain unchanged. ## Evidence A before-fix broadcaster check demonstrated that a session reader did not receive its targeted mention invalidation. The recipient exclusion was also traced to the broad-read role check. The corrected guest integration scenario exercises the real committed-input owner, broadcaster, and request dispatcher; its original pre-fix run had an unsuitable test host and is not counted as recipient baseline proof. The reviewed source at `8e189fc2` passed 1,131 distinct cases across 44 files. Its identical patch was replayed on `main` as `0f5a4f7`; 59 focused integration cases passed on that new head, covering both guest scopes, broadcaster serialization, sharing-target authority, and the sidebar lifecycle. Coverage includes both guest scope variants, automatic event arrival before a manual read, expected conversation/message identity, foreign-profile and owner-selector rejection, own dismissal across connections, replay protection, visibility loss/restoration, and role revocation. The existing sidebar lifecycle case also verifies guest activation makes no broad inventory requests. The test fixture preserves its profile subscriptions, and the new persistence case uses the existing host-owned database suite. Formatting parity, selected lint, the UI catalog check, and affected type checks pass. Each changed behavior file was measured with `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`: | File | Cases | Vitest wall time | Native test runner wall time | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `src/gateway/mention-inbox.guest.test.ts` | 2 | 22.16 s | 48.94 s | | `src/gateway/server-broadcast.serialization.test.ts` | 15 | 50.67 s | 54.13 s | | `ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-store.test.ts` | 33 | 2.91 s | 4.51 s | The 41 related importer files passed in 490.91 seconds for the native test batch. The guest scenario uses real persistence and dispatcher admission; its two case bodies took 3.468 and 1.558 seconds, with the remaining wall time in preparation and loading. Independent code and adversarial review is clean. Hosted CI also passed all 27 existing application Inbox cases. The two added guest cases took 2.204 and 1.083 seconds in CI. [Current CI run 39438477217](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39438477217) passed on `0f5a4f7`, including every selected UI, browser-test, and PostgreSQL shard. The earlier source run’s sole test failure was an inherited Custodian fixture defect, reproduced on its prerequisite base and already fixed on `main` by #177988; the replay includes that repair. An integrated test build demonstrates guest-to-admin and admin-to-eligible-guest automatic Inbox arrival before manual reads, opening without dismissal, exactly one entry after reload, and own-row dismissal. It includes the committed-mention delivery repair; it is not an isolated build of this PR. The original runtime and source-component correspondence are recorded below. Authenticated controls also passed: - A different profile’s dismissal request was a successful no-op; both owner entries remained. That conversation was visible to the caller, so this proves Inbox ownership isolation, not private-session denial. - One Admin UI dismissal sent `mentions.changed` to its other Admin tab, which automatically read the new view and removed only that entry without refresh. The unrelated entry remained once in both tabs. - A separate private draft was visible to its owner and Admin but hidden from a second guest. A deliberately forged recipient annotation through the authenticated API was rejected before commit, leaving history, run state, all target Inboxes, membership, and public sharing unchanged. This was an API negative control, not a natural UI send. Existing production-boundary regressions cover authority changes during pending work: [requester invalidation after list/dismiss preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f5a4f727d3683e979ebf7d0d8f5a187ff7a08a1/src/gateway/mention-inbox.test.ts#L127) returns `FORBIDDEN` and retains the entry; [visibility revocation before the real dismissal commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f5a4f727d3683e979ebf7d0d8f5a187ff7a08a1/src/gateway/mention-inbox.sharing-target.test.ts#L91) rejects the write and a reopened Inbox retains the original item; [recipient-role revocation before the real worker write](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f5a4f727d3683e979ebf7d0d8f5a187ff7a08a1/src/gateway/mention-inbox.test.ts#L207) produces no durable source or push. These assert final response/storage effects; no live roles or scopes were widened for proof. Final CI passed on the published head. Automated review rated the same head Platinum, with no findings or remaining merge requests. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Before: Admin types \@Gideon and the real picker reports No people found\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d9a2726-6c76-48ea-a3c8-1bf84ed8e06f) | ![Integrated after build: Admin opens the picker with \@ and the eligible guest is offered\.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fabdf731-56a7-4511-87fa-f94f6c94ac5f) | ### Integrated guest recipient: automatic arrival, Open, reload and own\-row dismissal https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2b2f821-0a61-462e-b411-45ffd775b342 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 46110002bf93db2af023262752dc5262a58dfd0d \(retained pre\-change recipient lookup\) - Exact head: `617f152e8112ae21211e84f3461d74efdff218b4` - Scenario: Admin can select an eligible guest, and the guest receives the mention automatically, opens it without dismissal, reconnects to one entry, and dismisses that own entry\. - Runtime/build: Native integrated build 617f152e / tree 61d29b1f, including recipient and scope changes from reviewed PR head 8e189fc2 and the committed\-mention delivery repair\. This is integrated evidence, not an isolated PR\-head deployment\. - Genuine before: Admin \@Gideon lookup returned no eligible people; no message was sent\. - Composed after: The same guest is offered; automatic Inbox entry appears before manual reads\. - Recipient lifecycle: Open retains the entry; reload has exactly one; own\-row Dismiss removes it\. - Comparison limits: Before query is \@Gideon; after query is \@\. Both original viewports are 1280x720 and output crops 768x238\. Sidebar widths and picker heights differ; this compares recipient eligibility, not search behavior or layout\. - Camera limits: Sender and recipient clips are separate unsynchronized cameras\. The recipient clip retains closed\-Inbox intervals as opaque frames; native receipts establish reload and send correlation\. - Ownership and cross\-tab: A foreign profile cannot dismiss another profile’s entry\. One owner UI dismissal updates its other tab automatically and retains the unrelated entry\. - Private recipient: A deliberately forged authenticated API annotation to an ineligible private\-session recipient is rejected before commit, with zero message/Inbox/membership effects; this is not a natural UI send\. - Genuine 461 pre\-change recipient capture retained; no recreated baseline or live downgrade - No pre\-change post\-send Inbox failure is claimed; eligibility prevented that send - After source/component correspondence and native activation qualified - Every selected recording frame was inspected; retained media digests are unchanged - Recipient and method\-scope changes match reviewed source; broader integrated runtime differences are disclosed - Authenticated foreign\-owner dismissal is a no\-op; current\-build cross\-tab dismissal removes only its target automatically - Private\-recipient API denial leaves message history, run state, Inbox and membership unchanged - Pending\-work requester/visibility/role authority is covered by existing production response and worker\-commit regressions - The identical patch replay passed focused integration checks; final CI and review remain separate landing gates ### Separate sender recording The sender and recipient clips show the same accepted scenario from separate cameras; their time axes are not synchronized. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccc9d621-ef78-4818-9137-27209a7c4070 ### Cross-tab dismissal controls These are separate cameras from one current-build action, not a pre-fix comparison. Both tabs belong to the same Admin profile. Tab A performs one UI dismissal; Tab B automatically removes that entry while preserving the other. Startup intervals are opaque and chronology is unchanged.
